posts.heading: September 20, 2026
posts.text:
The midday hours saw the Northern Cardinal assert vocal dominance, with detections peaking in the 13:00 hour while visual traffic on the feeder remained steady. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees continue to hold the seed tubes, accounting for the bulk of the 176 visits logged so far.

Weather has remained stable with a high of 27.9 C and light winds. A White-breasted Nuthatch provided the last visual sighting at 12:27, adding to the diversity of the 19 species identified today.

The Carolina Wren’s presence has been persistent through the afternoon, maintaining its position as a frequent vocalizer despite the shift in visual focus.

posts.heading: September 19, 2026
posts.text:
The day ended with 201 feeder visits, a figure that sits slightly above the recent seven-day average of 197.9, while the acoustic record of 224 detections remained quieter than the recent mean of 288.4. Tufted Titmice dominated the visual traffic with 99 visits, nearly half of all interactions, while Carolina Wrens provided the primary soundtrack with 116 detections. The station logged 23 species, comfortably exceeding the weekly mean of 17.7, with the first confident visual record at this station belonging to a Brown-headed Cowbird.

Regulars held steady, as the Carolina Wren, Tufted Titmouse, and Carolina Chickadee all appeared on the list of species recorded seven days in a row. Several one-off visitors added variety, including a Chimney Swift, an Orchard Oriole, and a Rose-breasted Grosbeak, each making single probable visits. A Red-shouldered Hawk called once during the noon hour, extending the week’s five-day streak for that species.

The lower number of detections compared to the recent average aligns with the change in audio source to the pi-mic on September 13, a shift that has been in place for the past week. The visual counts remain consistent with the station’s typical traffic, showing no disruption from the feeder installation on September 13.

posts.heading: September 18, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 90 feeder visits, a sharp drop from the seven-day average of 200.1. While the species count of 17 sat slightly above the weekly mean of 16.9, the visual traffic was sparse compared to the recent high-activity days. Regulars like the Carolina Wren and Tufted Titmouse remained consistent, holding steady counts that align with their presence every day this week.

Acoustic activity stayed above the previous average, with 17 species detected. The absence of Mourning Doves marked the first break in their seven-day streak. This quiet day follows the period after the new audio source was installed on September 13, which has stabilized detection records since the switch from the older microphone.

The day featured 8 confirmed visual visits, a fraction of the typical volume. No new species were recorded for the first time at this station. The final visual record came from a Carolina Wren, logged one minute after sunset.

posts.heading: September 17, 2026
posts.text:
September 17 added up to one of the busiest days of the week, with 302 feeder visits and 21 species recorded against a seven-day average of roughly 170 visits. Tufted Titmice remained the dominant feeder presence, accounting for 123 of the visits, while Carolina Chickadees and Ruby-throated Hummingbirds also held steady as regulars.

The acoustic record was dominated by Carolina Wrens, which contributed 132 detections, and Northern Cardinals, with 39. Several other species, including Blue Jays and Gray Catbirds, were heard frequently, while rare visitors like the Red-shouldered Hawk and White-eyed Vireo appeared briefly. All ten species that appear daily at this station were recorded again.

Activity at the station shifted following the installation of a new seed feeder earlier in the week, which replaced a unit previously causing detection problems. This change aligns with the rise in visual records, where Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees filled the majority of visits.

posts.heading: September 16, 2026
posts.text: The station closed out the day with 244 feeder visits and 23 species, figures that sit well above the seven-day average of 138 visits and 14 species. This high volume continues the trend established since the seed feeder was installed on September 13, replacing the unit that had been causing detection problems. Tufted Titmice remained the dominant visual presence, while Blue Jays led the acoustic record in the final hours.

posts.heading: September 15, 2026
posts.text:
September 15 was the busiest day of the past week, with 278 feeder visits and 21 species recorded, exceeding the recent seven-day averages. This surge follows the installation of the new seed feeder and pi-mic microphone on September 13. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees remained the primary visual presences, while Carolina Wrens dominated the audio logs with 126 detections.

The station logged its first confident visual records for Black-capped Chickadees and Eastern Phoebes. The daily roster included Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays, which have been recorded on all seven recent days. American Goldfinches have not appeared since earlier in the week.

posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text: The station’s activity outpaced the previous week’s average significantly, with 241 feeder visits and 16 species recorded compared to the prior seven-day mean of 63.6 visits and 10.0 species. This surge follows the installation of a new seed feeder on September 13, which resolved previous detection issues, and the switch to a new audio source the same morning. While Tufted Titmice remained the most frequent visual visitors with 97 confident sightings, Carolina Chickadees and Mourning Doves also contributed heavily to the visual counts.
